result.title: Learning to Extrapolate in Depth with Looped Transformers
result.summary: Looped transformers reuse a single block across iterations, raising a natural question: how far can a block trained at one depth be safely extrapolated to greater depths? We study this question for all-pairs graph connectivity, where harder graphs require longer-range information propagation. We show that under exchangeability and symmetric positive initialization, population training at depth K converges to an update rule governed by a single effective parameter that balances graph propagation against fitting structure unresolved at training depth. This trade-off creates a finite extrapolation window: too few test-time loops provide insufficient propagation, while too many eventually create false connections. We derive explicit endpoints for this window and bound the graph hardness solvable beyond training as a function of training depth and hardness. In particular, a test depth chosen solely from the training distribution can guarantee recovery on substantially harder graphs, with a certified depth gain that grows exponentially as training depth outpaces training hardness. Experiments validate the predicted windows and show how compute budget and initialization affect the optimal training depth.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 looped transformer 的深度外推问题：在 all-pairs 图连通性任务上，证明训练深度 K 下群体训练会收敛到由单一有效参数支配的更新规则，并给出有限外推窗口的两端与可保证更难图恢复的测试深度和认证深度收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「循环块复用—迭代次数在传播不足与伪连接之间的权衡」线索，可能与 LVR 中 loop 式 latent 状态更新、循环次数（STOP）选择及深度/长度泛化的预测工作区相关，可供核查；但任务为图连通性，非视觉多模态。
